newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Labour readies another attack on NZ First's Morgan.
newsitem.headline: Labour readies another attack on NZ First's Morgan.

text.p: The opposition Labour Party was on Wednesday readying another assault on New Zealand First Maori MP Tukoroirangi Morgan and his links with a pilot Maori language broadcaster.
Opposition Labour MP Trevor Mallard held a press conference on Wednesday to discuss an audio tape which he said was left on his desk late last week. He would not release it to the media.
"The tape is very damning," Mallard said.
Mallard has an arrangement with Television One's Holmes Show where further details are expected to be released late on Wednesday.

He said the tape had been left in an envelope with a cover note alleging it was an accidental recording of a conversation between Aotearoa Television Network (ATN) executive director Eric McPhee and director Morehu McDonald.
Mallard played Reuters a short extract from the hour long tape, which was of very poor sound quality.
He said he had met and spoken to both McPhee and McDonald previously and he was satisfied the tape was genuine and featured them.
A spokesman for NZ First leader Winston Peters said the party was not making any comment until it had investigated further.
Morgan could not be contacted for comment.
Labour leader Helen Clark alleged in Parliament last month that Morgan might have retained a shareholding in ATN held in trust for him after resigning as a director.
Cabinet in February reversed a decision to grant ATN an additional $4 million in funding when concerns emerged about financial controls at the station.

In Parliament on Wednesday Mallard said he wanted a select committee to investigate whether Morgan's brother-in-law, Maori Affairs Minister Tau Henare, knew Morgan still had an interest in ATN when cabinet originally decided to grant the station the $4 million.

Opposition MPs called for Morgan to resign in February after it was revealed he had spent $4,000 of ATN money on expensive clothes. Morgan said he had authority to spend the money, but staff at the station have denied this.
A Serious Fraud Office inquiry into the affairs of the station is yet to be completed.
